heroHeadline: Healey Delivers First Budget With Bank Tax Rise and Energy Bill Help as OBR Cuts Fiscal Headroom to £15bn
heroSubtitle: Chancellor John Healey delivered his first Budget on 28 October 2026, the first under Prime Minister Andy Burnham: £100 of energy bill help, higher bank tax and gambling machine duty, the fuel duty cut extended to July 2027 and a new Starter ISA. The House of Lords Library called the measures relatively small in fiscal terms, while the OBR forecast higher taxes, spending and borrowing than expected, with the fiscal rule met by a reduced £15bn margin.
footerNote: Data sourced from UK Parliament Hansard, The National Archives, ONS, Bank of England, Electoral Commission, NHS England, BBC, Reuters, FT, The Guardian, Bloomberg, Al Jazeera, CNN, CNBC, ITV News, SPICe, and major academic institutions including LSE, Chatham House, and the Resolution Foundation.
